Psychic You expand what your mind can accomplish.

Witch Your patron recognizes your need for flexibility and versatility, and grants you the power to prepare a wider range of simple spells.

Prepared You can prepare two additional cantrips each day.

Spontaneous Add two additional cantrips from your spell list to your repertoire.

entries.name: Conceal Spell
entries.effect:
Animist You speak with the unheard voice of the spirits.

Necromancer By shaping the magical energies and parameters of your spells through sheer concentration, you can simplify the incantations and gestures needed to spellcast, leaving them barely noticeable.

Witch Through sheer mental effort, you can simplify the incantations and gestures needed to spellcast, leaving them barely noticeable.

Wizard By shaping the magical energies and parameters of your spells all in your head through sheer concentration, you can simplify the incantations and gestures needed to spellcast, leaving them barely noticeable.

If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell, the spell gains the subtle trait, hiding the shining runes, sparks of magic, and other manifestations that would usually give away your spellcasting. The trait hides only the spell's spellcasting actions and manifestations, not its effects, so an observer might still see a ray streak out from you or see you vanish into thin air.

entries.name: Devoted Guardian
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect:
Requirements Your last action was to Raise a Shield.

You adopt a wide stance, ready to defend both yourself and your chosen ward. Select one adjacent creature. As long as your shield is raised and the creature remains adjacent to you, the creature gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their AC, or a +2 circumstance bonus if the shield you raised was a tower shield.

entries.name: Enhanced Familiar
entries.effect:
Animist You are able to materialize more of your attuned apparition's essence, creating a more powerful vessel for it to inhabit and aid you with.

Druid You infuse your familiar with additional primal energy, increasing its abilities.

Magus You infuse your familiar with more magical energy.

Sorcerer, Wizard, Witch You infuse your familiar with additional magical energy.

Thaumaturge By applying the best of multiple traditions of magic, you've found a more efficient way for your familiar to store its energy.

You can select four familiar or master abilities each day, instead of two.

Special Add the bonus familiar abilities you gain for being a witch to this amount. If your arcane thesis is Improved Familiar Attunement, your familiar's base number of familiar abilities, before adding any extra abilities from the arcane thesis, is four.

entries.name: Fane's Fourberie
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Pathfinder Society Guide
entries.effect:
Stella Fane has perfected a technique for using playing cards as weapons that's one part sleight of hand and one part magic.

When you enter this stance, choose whether to treat playing cards in your possession as daggers or darts; you can wield a playing card in all ways as the chosen weapon until the stance ends. As long as the majority of the deck remains in your possession, any cards that are lost or thrown can be found after 1 minute. Otherwise, the remaining cards are likely lost or destroyed.

A character who has this feat can enchant a single deck of playing cards as a magic weapon, etching fundamental and property runes directly onto the deck of cards.

entries.name: Intimidating Strike
entries.effect: Your blow not only wounds creatures but also shatters their confidence. Make a melee Strike. If you hit and deal damage, the target is Frightened 1, or Frightened 2 on a critical hit.

entries.name: Lightning Swap
entries.effect:
Exemplar You have practiced quickly switching between combat styles and the equipment needed for them, especially if you wield more than one weapon ikon. You Interact to stow any number of items from your hands, then draw up to two weapons or a shield and a weapon.

Fighter You have practiced quickly switching between combat styles and the equipment needed for them. You Interact to stow any number of items from your hands, then draw up to two weapons or a shield and a weapon.

entries.name: Poison Resistance
entries.effect:
Alchemist Repeated exposure to toxic reagents has fortified your body against poisons of all kinds.

Druid Your affinity for the natural world grants you protection against some of its dangers.

You gain poison resistance equal to half your level, and you gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against poisons.

entries.name: Quick Draw
entries.effect: You draw your weapon and attack with the same motion. You Interact to draw a weapon, then Strike with that weapon.

entries.name: Reliable Squire
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect: You know the path to victory isn't traveled alone, and you lend aid to your companions whenever you can. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to checks to Aid. If you roll a critical failure on a check to Aid, you get a failure instead.

entries.name: Resilient Mind
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect: You're firm in your convictions and have girded your mind against outside influence. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against mental effects. This bonus increases to +2 against mental effects originating from undead.

entries.name: United Assault
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect: Through countless battles, you've learned you're stronger when working alongside your allies. Make a Strike. Your Strike gains a circumstance bonus to damage rolls equal to the number of other different creatures that damaged the target since the end of the target's last turn, to a maximum of a +4 circumstance bonus.

entries.name: Boundless Reprisals
entries.effect:
Fighter With a sixth sense for the flow of combat, you can quickly react to any situation as required. At the start of each enemy's turn, you gain a reaction you can use only during that turn for any reaction from a fighter feat or class feature.

Guardian With a sixth sense for the flow of combat, you can quickly react to any situation as required. At the start of each enemy's turn, you gain a reaction you can use only during that turn for any reaction from a guardian feat or class feature.

entries.name: Spellshape Mastery
entries.effect: Altering your spells doesn't take any longer than casting them normally. You can use spellshape single actions as free actions.

entries.name: Barreling Charge
entries.effect: You rush forward, moving enemies aside to reach your foe. You Stride, attempting to move through your enemies' spaces. Roll an Athletics|Defense:Fortitude check and compare the result to the Fortitude DC of each creature whose space you attempt to move through during your Stride, moving through its space on a success but ending your movement before entering its space on a failure. You can then Strike, regardless of how your Stride ended. You can use Barreling Charge to Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim instead of Stride if you have the corresponding movement type.

entries.name: Bespell Strikes
entries.effect:
Frequency once per turn

Requirements Your most recent action was to cast a non-cantrip spell.

Oracle You siphon spell energy into one weapon you're wielding, or into one of your unarmed attacks, such as a fist. Until the end of your turn, the weapon or unarmed attack deals an extra 1d6 force damage and gains the divine trait if it didn't have it already. If the spell dealt a different type of damage, the Strike deals this type of damage instead (or one type of your choice if the spell could deal multiple types of damage).

Sorcerer You siphon spell energy into one weapon you're wielding or into one of your unarmed attacks, such as a fist. Until the end of your turn, the weapon or unarmed attack deals an extra 1d6 force damage and gains the trait of your bloodline's magical tradition if it didn't have it already. If the spell dealt a different type of damage, the Strike deals this type of damage instead (or one type of your choice if the spell could deal multiple types of damage).

Wizard You siphon spell energy into one weapon you're wielding, or into one of your unarmed attacks, such as a fist. Until the end of your turn, the weapon or unarmed attack deals an extra 1d6 force damage and gains the arcane trait if it didn't have it already. If the spell dealt a different type of damage, the Strike deals this type of damage instead (or one type of your choice if the spell could deal multiple types of damage).

entries.name: Brutal Crush
entries.effect:
Requirements Your last action dealt bludgeoning damage using an unarmed Strike granted by a morph or polymorph effect.

You've learned how to cloud your foes' minds with the brutal impact of your repeated attacks. Make an unarmed Strike against the same target. If the Strike hits and deals bludgeoning damage, the target is Stupefied 2 for 1 round (Stupefied 3 on a critical hit).

entries.name: Creature Comforts
entries.effect:
Trigger You become frightened.

Requirements You're under a morph or polymorph effect.

You've found comfort in the forms of other creatures, insulating yourself from feelings of fear. Reduce your frightened condition value by 1 (to a minimum of 0).

entries.name: Devrin's Dazzling Diversion
entries.effect: Devrin Arlos has a habit of using whatever is at hand to temporarily blind others in combat. Copying his technique, you make use of your cloak, the light reflecting from your weapon, a handful of flower petals, or some other physical distraction as part of your feint, leaving your opponent unable to see for a moment. When you successfully Feint a creature, it becomes Dazzled until the end of your turn. If you critically succeed, the creature is dazzled until the start of your next turn. The creature can use an Interaction to remove the dazzled condition. As normal, you can dazzle only creatures that use vision or a similar sense, as determined by the GM.

entries.name: Everstand Strike
entries.effect:
Requirements You are wielding a shield in two hands.

Your follow-up blow leaves you an opening to set your shield. Make a Strike with the wielded shield. If the Strike hits and deals damage, you also Raise your Shield.

entries.name: Farabellus Flip
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Pathfinder Society Guide
entries.effect:
Trigger An enemy targets you with a melee Strike.

Surprisingly agile even in a breastplate and carrying a full rucksack, Marcos Farabellus developed this evasive maneuver during one of his many adventures.

Flinging your body into a twisting somersault, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your AC against the triggering attack. If the attack still hits you, you can Step to an open space that's still within the triggering enemy's reach, turning the impact of the blow into momentum.

entries.name: Greenwatch Initiate
entries.effect: You've received the basic training developed for all Greenwatch recruits. You become an expert in Survival and gain the Experienced Tracker and Survey Wildlife skill feats.

entries.name: Haft Striker Stance
entries.effect:
Requirements You are wielding a two-handed hammer, spear, or polearm.

You enter a stance that allows you to leverage the haft of your weapon to brutal effect as an effective and frighteningly efficient weapon in its own right. You treat the haft of your wielded weapon as a simple weapon dealing 1D4[Bludgeoning] damage. The haft is in the club group and has the agile and finesse traits. The haft shares any fundamental runes attached to the main weapon, so long as it would normally qualify for them.

While in Haft Striker Stance, you can use feats and abilities that normally require you to be wielding two melee weapons each in a different hand, treating the haft as the second weapon, but you can't use abilities that require you to be wielding a two-handed weapon.

entries.name: Inspiring Resilience
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect:
Trigger You and at least one other creature become the target of a spell or effect with the emotion, fear, or mental trait that allows a saving throw, and you haven't rolled the save yet.

You show defiance in times of hardship and inspire your companions to persevere. Allies within 30 feet of you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to their Will save against the triggering effect, or a +2 circumstance bonus if the effect originated from an undead.

Effect: Inspiring Resilience

entries.name: Inured to Alchemy
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powder Keg
entries.effect:
Access You're from Alkenstar or the Mana Wastes.

You've developed control over how your body processes alchemical poisons and drugs. Each of your successful saving throws against an alchemical poison, a drug, or an addiction reduces the stage by 2, or by 1 for a virulent alchemical poison, drug, or addiction. Each critical success reduces the stage by 3, or by 2 for a virulent alchemical poison, drug, or addiction.

entries.name: Irezoko Tattoo
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Absalom, City of Lost Omens
entries.effect:
Access You are a member of the College of Mysteries

Your face bears an intricate magical tattoo known as the irezoko, a badge of your understanding of your chosen field of magic and a recognition of your advancement within Absalom's College of Mysteries. Choose a class that you are a member of that grants you access to a focus pool. When you take this feat, it gains the trait that applies to your chosen class. Once per day, you may concentrate upon the pattern of your irezoko to recover 1 Focus Point as a three-action activity.

entries.name: Knock Sense
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect: You attack carefully to knock some sense into a creature whose actions aren't their own. Make a Strike against a Confused ally. The Strike is nonlethal and doesn't take a -2 penalty for using a weapon without the nonlethal trait; if you hit and deal damage, your ally automatically succeeds at the flat check to remove the confused condition when taking damage.

entries.name: Masquerade of Seasons Stance
entries.effect: You have mastered the opening steps to the Masquerade of Seasons, a dance that channels the power of spring, summer, winter, and autumn. Choose one of the following traits: water, fire, void, or cold. You gain resistance 5 to damage dealt by effects with the chosen trait. You can use an action to reenter this stance at any time, changing the granted resistance to another of the available options. If you are at least 12th level, the granted resistance increases to be equal to half your level.

entries.name: Prayer-Touched Weapon
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect:
Frequency once per turn

Requirements Your most recent action was to cast a non-cantrip divine spell.

You coat a weapon you're wielding in prayers and the divine power given to you by your deity. Until the end of your turn, the weapon deals an extra 1D6[Vitality] damage. As usual for vitality damage, this damage harms only undead and creatures with void healing.

entries.name: Rip and Tear
entries.effect:
Requirements Your last action dealt piercing or slashing damage using an unarmed Strike granted by a morph or polymorph effect.

You've learned to debilitate your enemies in the same way a hunter tears at their prey. Make an unarmed Strike against the same target. If the Strike hits and deals piercing or slashing damage, the target takes an additional 1d6 persistent bleed damage. If you're at least 12th level, increase this to 2d6 persistent bleed damage.

entries.name: Running Reload
entries.effect: You can reload your weapon on the move. You Stride, Step, or Sneak, then Interact to reload.

entries.name: Sacral Lord
entries.effect:
By right of ritual or sheer stubbornness, you have claimed rulership of the land. Claim a defined territory, such as a small section of forest or river, or a district of a larger city. Within its borders, you can cast Detect Magic, Guidance, and Sigil as innate divine cantrips, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [[/act make-an-impression]] on creatures that have the celestial, fiend, fey, monitor, or spirit traits.

Special You and your land are linked. Changes to one mirror themselves on the other—if you're depressed, gray rain and clammy mist might set in. These effects have no immediate mechanical impact, but they might give clues about problems afflicting the land.

entries.name: Scout's Warning
entries.effect:
Trigger You are about to roll a Perception, Stealth, or Survival check for initiative.

You visually or audibly warn your allies of danger, granting them each a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative rolls, or a +2 circumstance bonus if you're using the Scout exploration activity. Depending on whether you use gestures or call out, this action gains either the visual or the auditory trait, respectively.

Effect: Scout'S Warning

entries.name: Swipe
entries.effect:
You make a wide, arcing swing. Make a single melee Strike and compare the attack roll result to the ACs of up to two enemies, each of whom must be within your melee reach and adjacent to the other. Roll damage only once and apply it to each creature you hit. A Swipe counts as two attacks for your multiple attack penalty.

If you're using a weapon with the sweep trait, its modifier applies to all your Swipe attacks.

entries.name: Twin Parry
entries.effect:
Requirements You are wielding two melee weapons, one in each hand.

You use your two weapons to parry attacks. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, or a +2 circumstance bonus if either weapon has the parry trait. You lose this circumstance bonus if you no longer meet this feat's requirement.

entries.name: Undying Conviction
entries.effect:
Your presence has a bolstering effect on your undead minions. Undead creatures under your control and within a Emanation|Distance:30 around you gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws to resist vitality damage and to Will saving throws to resist effects that would make them controlled.

Effect: Under Control

Effect: Undying Conviction

Special This feat has the trait matching your spellcasting tradition.

entries.name: Defy Fey
entries.effect: You are keen to the wiles of the fey and can usually shake off their magic. Whenever you fail, but don't critically fail, a save against a spell with a duration of at least 1 round cast by a fey creature, you can attempt a second save against the original DC at the start of your next turn to end any lingering effects the spell might have. This can end persistent damage caused by a spell but can't reverse any effects that have been resolved already (such as damage dealt when the spell was cast).

entries.name: Detonating Spell
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect: Your spell becomes volatile and explosive. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that deals damage to a single target and the spell successfully damages that target, the spell explodes, dealing splash damage equal to the rank of the spell cast to adjacent creatures. Unlike normally, this splash damage doesn't apply to the target. The splash damage dealt is of the same type the spell deals.

entries.name: Divine Emissary
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect:
Your familiar is a divine emissary, sent to you by your deity or patron and infused with celestial powers. You can select one additional familiar ability each day, which must be one of the following divine emissary familiar abilities. You can't select more than one divine emissary familiar ability at a time.

  • Erudite
  • Luminous
  • Medic
  • Radiant

entries.name: Fey Tracker
entries.effect: You are exceptionally skilled at noticing the subtle techniques fey use to avoid notice. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Survival checks to Track fey creatures, to Perception checks to Seek for Hidden fey, and to your Perception DC to resist a fey creature's attempt to Create A Diversion.

entries.name: Fight or Flight
entries.effect:
Access You're from the Shackles

Trigger You gain the frightened condition.

You've learned to make use of the surge of adrenaline that comes with fear. You can make a melee Strike against a creature that gave you the frightened condition if it's within range, or you can Stride up to your speed away from the effect or creature that gave you the frightened condition.

entries.name: Intensified Element Stance
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Tian Xia Character Guide
entries.effect:
Access Tian Xia origin

Requirements You were the recipient of elemental medicine (see Prepare Elemental Medicine) during your last daily preparations.

You expend the elemental medicine in your body to empower your attacks, though you can't consume any more elemental medicine until the next day. While in Intensified Element Stance, your strikes and damaging spells deal an additional 1d6 damage against certain creatures, depending on the type of elemental medicine you expended. If the person who crafted the elemental medicine expended was legendary in the skill they used, increase this damage to 2d6.

  • Earth acid damage against water creatures
  • Fire fire damage against metal creatures and constructs that are primarily metallic
  • Metal electricity damage against wood or plant creatures and constructs primarily made of wood or plant matter
  • Water sonic damage against fire creatures
  • Wood cold damage against earth creatures and constructs that are primarily made of rock or earth

entries.name: Pain Tolerance
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powder Keg
entries.effect:
Access You're from Alkenstar or the Mana Wastes.

You gain resistance to mental damage equal to half your level and a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against effects that would make you Clumsy, Drained, or Enfeebled.

entries.name: Pirouette
entries.effect:
Requirements You're in Masquerade of Seasons Stance.

Trigger An enemy targets you with a Strike.

You twirl gracefully, spinning on one foot to evade your opponent's attack. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses you, you can immediately Step. If the attack hits you anyway, reduce the damage it deals by an amount equal to half your level; this reduction in damage is applied after calculating immunities, resistances, and weakness.

entries.name: Reactive Strike
entries.effect:
Trigger A creature within your reach uses a manipulate action or a move action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it's using.

You swat a foe that leaves an opening. Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature. If your attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a manipulate action, you disrupt that action. This Strike doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike.

entries.name: Reflexive Shield
entries.effect:
You can use your shield to fend off explosions and the like. When you Raise your Shield, you gain your shield's circumstance bonus to Reflex saves.

Special If you have the Shield Block reaction, damage you take as a result of a Reflex save can trigger that reaction, even if the damage isn't physical damage.

entries.name: Shield Wall
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect:
Trigger Your shield is raised and an adjacent ally Raises a Shield.

You use your shield in tandem with an ally's, forming a barricade. Both you and the triggering creature have Standard Cover as long as you remain adjacent to each other and you both have your shields raised; when this is no longer the case, the effect ends. You and your ally can't use this cover to Hide, as it's obvious you're standing there holding your shields, but you and your ally can use it to Take Cover. Normally, if you and your ally don't move, Shield Wall lasts until the beginning of your next turn, when your shield is no longer raised.

entries.name: Shield Warden
entries.effect: When you have a shield raised, you can use your Shield Block reaction when an attack is made against an ally adjacent to you. If you do, the shield prevents that ally from taking damage instead of preventing you from taking damage, following the normal rules for Shield Block.

entries.name: Skirmish Strike
entries.effect: Your feet and weapon move in tandem. Either Step and then Strike, or Strike and then Step.

entries.name: Steady Spellcasting
entries.effect: Confident in your technique, you don't lose spells easily. If a reaction would disrupt your spellcasting action, attempt a Flat|Showdc:All|Dc:15. If you succeed, your action isn't disrupted.

entries.name: Stella's Stab and Snag
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Pathfinder Society Guide
entries.effect:
Requirements You are wielding a piercing or slashing melee weapon.

You dart towards your opponent, seeking to stab them and slice their purse-strings with a single movement. Stride up to your Speed; this movement does not trigger reactions triggered by movement. At any point during this movement you can Strike an opponent within reach. If this Strike is successful, you can attempt a Thievery check to Steal from the target.

entries.name: Blind-Fight
entries.effect:
Fighter, Rogue, Investigator Your battle instincts make you more aware of Concealed and Invisible opponents.

Ranger Your heightened senses allow you to instinctively detect unseen opponents.

You don't need to succeed at a flat check to target concealed creatures. You're not Off Guard to creatures that are Hidden from you (unless you're off-guard to them for reasons other than the hidden condition), and you need only a successful Flat|Showdc:All|Dc:5 to target a hidden creature.

While you're adjacent to an Undetected creature of your level or lower, it is instead only hidden from you.

entries.name: Cannonball Fall
entries.effect:
You've learned how to make a quick descent with a sudden stop—directly on an enemy. You intentionally fall onto an enemy within 10 feet of you horizontally and can accurately target them from up to a height equal to 5 feet times your level. You take damage as normal; the enemy must attempt a Reflex|Against:Class save against your class DC with the following results, instead of the usual rules for falling on a creature. If an ability reduces the amount of damage you take from falling, the enemy's damage is based on the damage you would have taken before that reduction. In addition, if you have a means of controlling your descent, such as holding onto a rope or sliding down an adjacent wall, you do not land Prone even if you take damage from the fall.

Critical Success The enemy takes no damage.

Success The enemy takes bludgeoning damage equal to one-quarter the falling damage you took.

Failure The creature takes bludgeoning damage equal to half the falling damage you took and is knocked prone.

Critical Failure The creature takes the same amount of bludgeoning damage you took from the fall, is knocked prone, and is Stunned 1.

entries.name: Can't You See?
entries.effect: The eye rebels, the mind recoils—no matter how much those who can see you try to explain what's there, their friends' gazes just skitter over you, like a bird afraid to land. A character who attempts to Point Out your location must attempt a Flat|Dc:14. If they fail, their allies misunderstand them and aren't sure where you are. On a critical failure, their allies think they pointed you out in a different location entirely, chosen by the GM. Similarly, when a creature critically fails to [[/act seek]] you while you're Hidden to or Undetected by it, it thinks you're in a different location chosen by the GM. In either case, you appear to be hidden to a creature that thinks you're in a different location, though you're actually undetected by it for targeting and further uses of the Seek action.

entries.name: Chaotic Spell
entries.effect:
This is the secret of chaotic magic - your foe can hardly predict and counter your moves if you yourself have no idea what will happen. If the next action you use is to Cast a Spell that deals acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage, roll a [[/r 1d6]]{d6}. The spell's damage type changes to the type below associated with the result of the roll, and each creature who is damaged by the spell takes the listed additional effect.

1 (Acid): Sickened 1

2 (Cold): –10 ft. penalty to all Speeds until the end of your next turn

3 (Electricity): Off Guard until the end of your next turn

4 (Fire): Persistent fire damage equal to the spell's rank

5 (Force): No added effect

6 (Sonic): Deafened for 2 rounds

entries.name: Eerie Environs
entries.effect: The natural world can be scary to those not used to it—and you make it scarier still. If you're Hidden from a creature, you can attempt to [[/act demoralize]] it without losing your hidden condition—imitating the sounds of strange beasts or causing the foliage to rustle menacingly. When you do so, you don't take a penalty to your check if the target doesn't understand your language.

entries.name: Eerie Traces
entries.effect:
The tracks you leave behind are strange, somehow disconcerting and unnerving—they might travel backward, or through places no one would think to pass through. You change your tracks into eerie traces, moving up to half your travel speed as you do so. You don't need to attempt a Survival check to change your tracks, but anyone tracking you must attempt a Will save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC.

Success The tracker is unaffected.

Failure The tracker becomes Frightened 1 for as long as it follows your tracks. This condition doesn't decrease until the tracker stops following you, and it comes back if the tracker resumes following your tracks. If the tracker enters into an encounter with you after following your tracks, it begins the encounter frightened 1.

Critical Failure As failure, but your disturbing traces cause the tracker to be Frightened 2 instead.

entries.name: Grand Dance
entries.effect:
Requirements You're in Masquerade of Seasons Stance.

You can summon the full magic of Bhopan's grand dance. Stride up to your Speed; during this Stride, you can walk on air as if it were solid ground. You can ascend and descend in this way at a maximum of a 45-degree angle. You must end your Stride on a surface that can support you or you fall.

entries.name: Greenwatch Veteran
entries.effect:
Trigger Your turn starts, and you're in combat against a creature you spent at least 10 minutes Tracking.

Your time spent tracking your target allows you to quickly identify its weaknesses and relay them to your allies. Attempt a Recall Knowledge check against the creature you were Tracking. On a success, you always know the creature's greatest weakness and highest resistance or immunity, in addition to any other information the check would typically provide. You immediately use a quick series of hand gestures to signal this information to any allies who can see you.

entries.name: Helt's Spelldance
entries.effect:
Ranik Helt knows a special technique to hide his spells as part of a performance, and you've learned this technique. Ostentatiously performing, you move across the battlefield, taking foes aback and creating an opening for your spell. Attempt a Performance|Against:Perception check against all observers' Perception DCs. Then, Stride once or twice. During this movement, you don't trigger reactions that are triggered by your movement from the creatures against which you succeeded on your Performance check.

After your movement, you can Cast a Spell. If you used one Stride, you can cast either a 1-action or a 2-action spell; if you used two Strides, you can only cast a 1-action spell. If you critically succeed on your check against any creature, they take a –1 circumstance penalty to their saving throws against any spell you cast as part of your Helt's Spelldance due to your distracting performance.

Effect: Helt'S Spelldance

All creatures that observed you become temporarily immune to your Helt's Spelldance for 10 minutes.

entries.name: Impassable Wall Stance
entries.effect: You refuse to let foes past your guard. As long as you are in this stance, when you critically hit with an Reactive Strike triggered by a move action, you disrupt that move action.

entries.name: Incredible Familiar
entries.effect:
Thaumaturge By taking the best parts of each magical tradition, you've found a way to grant your familiar even more abilities than other familiars.

Witch Your familiar is imbued with even more magic than other familiars.

You can select a base of six familiar or master abilities each day, instead of four.

Special Add the bonus familiar abilities you gain for being a witch to this amount.

entries.name: Knight's Retaliation
entries.publication_title: Pathfinder Lost Omens Knights of Lastwall
entries.effect:
Trigger An undead creature within your reach critically fails a Strike against you.

You knock the enemy's blow aside and twist, unbalancing your foe. You attempt to Disarm, Shove, or Trip the triggering creature.

entries.name: Know-It-All
entries.effect:
Bard When you succeed at a check to Recall Knowledge, you gain additional information or context. When you critically succeed at a check to Recall Knowledge, you get additional information or context or can ask an additional follow-up question (the GM chooses which).

Thaumaturge Having heard and scrutinized every rumor or story in the book, you know for a fact that if you've heard something at all, you've probably heard about it at great length. When you succeed or critically succeed at a check to Recall Knowledge, you can ask an additional follow-up question. At the GM's discretion, you might gain even more additional context than normal.

entries.name: Quick Shield Block
entries.effect: You can bring your shield into place with hardly a thought. At the start of each of your turns, you gain an additional reaction that you can use only to Shield Block.

entries.name: Sudden Leap
entries.effect:
Barbarian You swing at a foe while mid-leap.

Fighter You make an impressive leap and swing while you soar.

Make a Leap, High Jump, or Long Jump and attempt one melee Strike at any point during your jump. Immediately after the Strike, you fall to the ground if you're in the air, even if you haven't reached the maximum distance of your jump. If the distance you fall is no more than the height of your jump, you take no damage and land upright.

When attempting a High Jump or Long Jump during a Sudden Leap, determine the jump distance using Long Jump's rules, and change your maximum distance to double your Speed.

Special If you have Felling Strike, you can use Felling Strike instead of a normal Strike. This doesn't change the number of actions Sudden Leap takes.

entries.name: Unseen Passage
entries.effect:
Frequency once per day

You have mastered a magical technique for moving through dangerous woodlands unseen. You can cast Vanishing Tracks as an innate primal spell heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.

entries.name: Backup Runic Enhancement
entries.effect: While you are not a spellcaster, you have a working knowledge of the most fundamental runic magic. You can cast the Sigil cantrip as an innate spell at will. In addition, choose either Runic Body or Runic Weapon. You can cast this spell once per day as an innate spell. The rank of these spells is equal to half your level, rounded up, and the tradition can be any tradition for which you are at least trained in the related skill (Arcana for arcane, Nature for primal, Occultism for occult, and Religion for divine).

entries.name: Engraving Strike
entries.effect:
Requirements You are wielding a melee weapon.

You draw a rune onto the surface of your weapon in reverse, the mark branding or bruising itself into your target at the moment of impact. Make a melee strike with the weapon. On a success, you Trace a Rune onto the target of the Strike.

entries.name: Glyph Familiar
entries.effect: You have taken a living rune as a familiar to aid you in your adventures. You gain a familiar. You choose one familiar or master ability per day instead of two, but your familiar also always has three additional familiar abilities: construct, flier, and tough.

entries.name: Remote Detonation
entries.effect: You whisper an invocation over your ammunition as you shoot it, and the hissing of the projectile sounds just like your murmured voice. Make a ranged Strike that uses physical ammunition against a target within the first range increment of your weapon. If it hits, you Invoke Runes on the target as whisper of the ammunition's flight sets off the runes. You can invoke up to two runes this way, but all the runes must be on the target of your Strike. On a critical hit, the target takes a –1 circumstance penalty on any saving throws against the runes invoked by your Remote Detonation.

entries.name: Rune-Singer
entries.effect:
You practice the lost art of using music to guide your rune-carving, singing the runes into existence as much as crafting them. You can use Performance instead of Crafting when attempting Crafting checks related to runes.

Once per 10 minutes, you can Trace a Rune with song alone. When you do, you use the 2-action version of Trace Rune as a single action without needing an artisan's toolkit, and you remove the action's manipulate trait. You don't need to be able to move your hands when Tracing a Rune using song, but you do need to be able to sing in a clear voice.

entries.name: Rune Ward
entries.effect:
Trigger You are targeted by a spell.

Requirements You are trained in the skill associated with the tradition of the triggering spell (Arcana for arcane, Nature for primal, Occultism for occult, and Religion for divine).

You quickly sketch a rune in the air to gain a modicum of protection against the triggering magic. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your saving throw and AC against the spell.

entries.name: Seek the Hidden Glyphs
entries.effect:
You are well-versed in the use of magical runes in traps and hazards. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find magical traps. Even if you aren't Searching, you get a check to find magical traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap. As long as you are holding or wearing an artisan's toolkit, you can use Crafting instead of Thievery to disable a magical trap ([[/act disable-device skill=crafting]]), treating your proficiency in Crafting as your proficiency in Thievery for requirements.

In addition, if you trigger a trap by critically failing a check to Disable it, you can Trace a Rune on yourself as a reaction, gaining the benefits of the rune before the trap affects you.

entries.name: Smithing Weapons
entries.effect: Though you are an artisan, you are well versed in using the tools of your trade to fend off enemies. While wielding a weapon in the hammer, knife, or pick weapon group, you can use that weapon to etch runes without an Artisan'S Toolkit. Additionally, a Strike with a hammer, knife, or pick deals 1 additional fire damage to an enemy bearing one of your runes as sparks fly on impact like a hammer to an anvil.

entries.name: Chain of Words
entries.effect:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

You see the thin lines of magic between your creations, and you can exploit that connection with a small shift of power from one rune to another. You Invoke two Runes within 60 feet. In addition to the runes' normal effects, a chain of glowing script flows between them, dealing Level/2)))D6[Force|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in a straight line between them with a Reflex|Against:Runesmith|Basic|Options:Area Effect,Inflicts:Immobilized saving throw; creatures bearing the invoked runes are not in the area of this line. A creature who critically fails its save is also Immobilized for 1 round or until it [[/act escape]]{Escapes}, as the runes seal its movements. The DC to Escape is your class DC. At 12th level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d6.

entries.name: Clashing Compound Invocation
entries.effect:
As you invoke runes from disparate traditions of magic, their diametrically opposed effects repel each other in a destructive backlash. You Invoke two Runes, which must be from opposed traditions of magic; either 1 arcane and 1 divine rune, or 1 occult and 1 primal rune. In addition to the runes' normal effects, one creature within 30 feet of both invoked runes must also attempt a Fortitude|Against:Runesmith|Options:Inflicts:Sickened saving throw as destructive magical harmonics clash.

Success The target is Sickened 1, but if it spends a single action attempting to recover, it automatically succeeds.

Failure The target is sickened 1.

Critical Failure The target is Sickened 2.

entries.name: Overloaded Ammunition
entries.effect:
You can tenuously bind power into arrows or sling stones to transform them into explosive missiles. During your daily preparations, you can lay power-containing runes upon two pieces of mundane ammunition to transform them into Explosive Ammunition. The DC of the explosive ammunition is equal to your class DC. The binding on the powder is unstable, and the ammunition burns itself to ash by your next daily preparations if not used. This ammunition has no value if sold.

At 14th level, you create Greater Explosive Ammunition instead.

entries.name: Prodigal Rune-Singer
entries.effect: You have mastered the art of singing your runes. You can Trace a Rune with song once per round instead of once per 10 minutes.

entries.name: Runic Correspondence
entries.effect:
You can write a message that travels long distances at the speed of thought. Once per day, you can take 1 minute to write a message of 25 words or fewer anywhere that can, at least momentarily, hold writing (such as on a piece of parchment, drawn in the sand, or lightly scratched onto soft metal). When you are finished, mentally picture one creature you know well. If the target creature is on the same plane as you, your message appears in their line of sight on any surface that can hold writing. It can be seen by only the target, and the target can read the message even if you don't share a language. The message disappears once the target reads it, but the creature can respond by spending 1 minute to write their own message of 25 words or fewer in the same way. You instantly receive that message when it is finished, and you can read it even if you don't share a language.

If you spend 10 minutes writing your message instead, you can include a rune from your runic repertoire. If the target is willing, after reading your message, you Trace the Rune on the target to last for up to 10 minutes. When you receive the creature's reply, you can Invoke that Rune as a free action.

entries.name: Astral Compound Invocation
entries.effect:
Invoking runes from two schools of magic that both manipulate the intangible realm of thought results in waves of mental interference that stagger your foes. You Invoke two Runes; one must be an arcane rune, and one must be an occult rune.

In addition to the runes' normal effects, one creature within 30 feet of both invoked runes must attempt a Will|Against:Runesmith|Options:Inflicts:Stupefied saving throw.

Critical Success The target is unaffected by the compound invocation.

Success The target is Stupefied 1 until the end of your next turn.

Failure The target is Stupefied 2 until the end of your next turn.

Critical Failure The target is Stupefied 3 until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Distant Invocation
entries.effect: Your connection to your runes stretches over even greater distances. You add 30 feet to the range of any of your invocation abilities (typically increasing the range from 30 to 60 feet).

entries.name: Expanded Glossary
entries.effect: You have memorized more runes than many in your craft. Add two runes of 9th level or lower to your runic repertoire.

entries.name: Orbiting Runestone
entries.effect:
You create a runestone that floats around you, and you Trace a Rune with a damaging invocation on it even if the rune could not normally be applied to an object. The runestone has 10 Hit Points. Each time a creature successfully Strikes you, attempt a Flat|Dc:11|Showdc:All. On a success, the runestone blocks the attack, so the attack first damages the runestone and then applies any remaining damage to you. If this damage reduces the runestone to 0 Hit Points, it explodes outward toward the attacker. If the attacker is within 15 feet, the rune etched upon the runestone invokes automatically, applying its invocation effect to the attacker. The attacker is the only one affected by the invocation, even if the rune could normally affect multiple creatures.

The runestone's magic is capable of maintaining the traced rune for up to 1 minute as it floats around you, at which point the rune fades and the runestone shatters. You can maintain only a single orbiting rune at any given time. If you try to create a second, the first one shatters.

entries.name: Dance of Bloody Ink
entries.effect:
Requirements You're wielding a melee weapon that bears a rune.

As you lash out, your weapon is your brush, wounds forming words of power in your target's flesh. You Invoke a Rune on a melee weapon you are wielding and Strike. Then, you can Step and Strike again with the same weapon. If the second Strike hits, you Trace a Rune onto the target of the Strike. Both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but you do not increase your penalty until you have made all your attacks.

entries.name: Define the Canvas
entries.effect:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

You produce rune-inscribed stones, which whirl in the air before darting away to form a perimeter for a runic canvas. The canvas is a Type:Burst|Distance:20 on the ground centered on a corner in your space. As long as you're in or adjacent to the canvas, you can Trace a Rune directly into the ground, which causes the rune to expand across the entire space, tracing it onto any number of eligible targets within the area. The canvas lasts for 1 minute.

entries.name: Henge Gate
entries.effect:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

You hold a rune in your heart and strike the earth, causing two standing stones to rise nearby, your chosen rune carved upon their surfaces and blazing in the air above them. The stones each appear in an unoccupied 5-foot space within 30 feet of you and within 15 feet of each other. When you raise the henge gate, choose one rune that can be drawn on a creature to carve into the stones. If you or an ally makes a successful ranged Strike using physical ammunition and that attack passes through the henge gate, the ammunition gains that rune in flight and automatically traces it on the target. The henge gate lasts for 1 minute.

entries.name: Unerring Runic Attraction
entries.effect: Your runes act as beacons for your arrows and bolts. Make a ranged Strike against a foe you're aware of that's currently bearing a rune and within your first range increment. The ammunition homes in on your target, even going around corners. Your Strike doesn't require line of sight, ignores the target's Concealed condition, and ignores all circumstance bonuses to AC granted from cover and shields.

entries.name: By Your Name
entries.effect:
Frequency once per hour

Requirements You must know the target's name.

In a moment of inspiration, you understand the target perfectly, allowing you to craft a rune that draws effects to the target by their very name. Attempt a Crafting check against a standard DC of the target creature's level. Regardless of the outcome, you can't attempt to use By Your Name against the target again for 24 hours.

Critical Success You understand the target's runic name and temporarily learn how to write their name as a special diacritic rune. This diacritic rune magnifies the effects of the base rune when targeting the named creature. When the rune is invoked, the target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to their saving throw against the effects of the base rune, and if the base rune deals damage, it gains a status bonus to its damage equal to half your level. The inspiration used to understand this diacritic rune fades quickly, and you forget how to use the diacritic rune after 1 minute.

Success As critical success, but the rune doesn't grant a bonus to damage.

entries.name: Maze of Runes
entries.effect: You can trap a foe in a twisting, extradimensional labyrinth of ever-shifting runes. You can cast Quandary once per day as an innate spell. The rank of this spell is equal to half your level rounded up, and the tradition can be any tradition for which you are at least legendary in the related skill. Instead of the usual skill checks to solve the puzzle, the target of your quandary can attempt a Perception|Against:Runesmith check, a Society check to [[/act decipher-writing]], or a check in the skill related to the tradition of the spell. When you Sustain this spell, you can also Trace a Rune or Invoke one Rune on the target creature as if it were adjacent to you.

entries.name: Return Unto Runes
entries.effect:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

Trigger An enemy targets you with a spell attack or other magical attack against your AC.

You attempt to deconstruct an incoming spell into its individual magical components, storing them temporarily as a rune. You gain a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If the attack misses, the spell becomes sealed in a rune, which floats around you. Until the end of your next turn, you can Trace this Rune onto a creature as normal. This rune doesn't have an effect until it's invoked. When the rune is invoked, the rune-bearer is affected by the spell or magical attack captured in the rune. Make a check, using your class DC – 10 as the modifier against the rune-bearer's AC to determine the effects.

entries.name: Runesight
entries.effect: It is impossible for those bearing runes to hide from you. You can sense the presence of all rune-bearers within 60 feet as a precise sense.

entries.name: Annihilating Compound Invocation
entries.effect: Each tradition of magic holds sway over two of the four essences that make up all of creation, and so by invoking runes from each tradition at once, you can pull from the four corners of magic to unravel anything. You invoke four runes of your choice, each of which must be from a different tradition of magic. In addition to the runes' normal effects, one creature within 30 feet of all invoked runes must attempt a Fortitude|Against:Runesmith|Basic saving throw, taking 10D4[Force] damage on a failure as destructive magical reverberations clash in their body. If reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage or by the damage of any of the runes invoked, the creature's body is torn apart into glowing script that describes the creature to the smallest detail, leaving no remains as the letters fade. The creature's gear is unharmed.

entries.name: Living Lexicon
entries.effect: Your knowledge of runes knows no bounds. You add an additional rune to your runic repertoire of any level. Additionally, each day during your daily preparations, you can swap any one rune in your runic repertoire with another rune of the same level.

entries.name: Unbounded Invocations
entries.effect: Your words can shake the very foundations of the world. When you Invoke Runes, you can invoke any number of runes within 30 feet instead of just two.

entries.name: Enhanced Glyph Familiar
entries.effect: Your living rune is imbued with more magical power. You can select two familiar or master abilities each day instead of one. In addition, when you Trace a Rune with a single action, your target can be adjacent to your familiar instead of adjacent to you. Your familiar must be within 30 feet of you for this benefit.

entries.name: Fortifying Knock
entries.effect:
Requirements You are wielding a shield.

Your shield is a natural canvas for your art. In one motion, you Raise A Shield and Trace a Rune on your shield.

entries.name: Invisible Ink
entries.effect: After your rune is drawn, it flares once and then fades, leaving only the barest mark. When you apply a rune on an object or creature, you can Conceal An Object as a free action to hide that rune. If a creature would get a chance to find the rune, the GM uses your Crafting DC instead of your Stealth DC.

entries.name: Pattern Flight
entries.effect: You place a bit of magic in a physical projectile, causing it to fly in a runic pattern through the air once you loose it. Make a ranged Strike against a target within your weapon's first range increment. Because of the erratic nature of its flight, this Strike ignores any circumstance bonus to AC from cover. After your Strike, you can Trace a Rune on one target in a straight line between you and the target of your Strike (including the original target).

entries.name: Runic Tattoo
entries.effect:
By drawing your favorite rune in your flesh, you know you'll never be without it. Choose one rune you know, which you apply as a tattoo to your body. The rune is always etched on your body and does not count toward your maximum limit of etched runes. You can invoke this rune like any of your other runes, but once invoked, the rune fades significantly and is drained of power until your next daily preparations.

You can magically alter your runic tattoo to change it to another rune you know (or remove it altogether) with 1 day of downtime.

entries.name: Forge New Word
entries.effect:
At the pinnacle of your art, you have forged a new great rune of power, a new ideal expression or utterance to be added to the craft. You create a rune and add it to your runic repertoire. When you gain this feat, choose a spell of 4th rank or lower. It must be common, or you must otherwise have access to it. The spell must take 1 or 2 actions to cast. You can choose a variable-action spell, deciding when you create the rune whether the rune uses the 1-action or 2-action version of the spell. Name your rune. This rune has the unique trait and a magical trait of your choosing (arcane, divine, occult, or primal).

This rune can be drawn on a creature or object, regardless of what the spell can target. When invoked, this rune has the effect of the chosen spell. The rune-bearer is the point of origin for the spell's effect; calculate range and cover from its space. If the spell has targets, you decide who or what the spell targets, and the rune-bearer is a possible target if your chosen spell can target it. If the spell can affect only you (such as Translocate), invoking it affects only you, and has no effect if the rune is drawn anywhere other than on you. If the spell requires a spell attack roll, use your class DC – 10 in place of the spell attack modifier. If your chosen spell has a duration and that duration is longer than 1 minute, the invoked rune's duration is 1 minute instead.

entries.name: Generational Rune-Singer
entries.effect: You are a once-in-a-generation genius. You can Trace a Rune with song at will and at a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Shades of Meaning
entries.effect: As the gap between your intention and your words becomes almost nothing, you find that you don't need to consciously draw the diacritic marks that would embellish or modify your runes. As you draw a rune, it continues to grow outward like a living thing, applying the exact accent or stress mark you intended for it to have. Whenever you etch or Trace a Rune, you can choose to also apply one diacritic rune you know to it as part of the same action.

entries.name: Stone Forge of the First
entries.effect:
Frequency once per day

You conjure forth a massive stone forge within 30 feet that occupies a 15-foot cube in empty spaces on the ground. The forge lasts for 1 minute before crumbling into dust. The forge amplifies the power of runes in a Type:Emanation|Distance:60. The duration of a traced rune doesn't elapse while it's within the emanation but resumes once the rune is outside the emanation. Additionally, runes invoked within the forge's emanation don't fade, but instead become faint. Faint runes maintain their passive benefits but can't be invoked again.

entries.name: Artist's Attendance
entries.effect: Your runes call you to better attend to your art. Stride twice. If you end your movement within reach of a creature that is bearing one of your runes, you can Trace a Rune upon that creature or another target adjacent to you. You can use Artist's Attendance while Burrowing, Climbing, Flying, or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

entries.name: Ghostly Resonance
entries.effect: Your runes don't just draw power from the world of the spirits—they can let even the most mundane objects harm spirits as well. When you etch or trace a divine or occult rune on a weapon or creature, you can grant it the Ghost Touch weapon property rune. For a weapon, this doesn't count toward the weapon's limit on property runes. For a creature, the rune applies to all unarmed Strikes the creature makes. This benefit lasts as long as the rune remains.

entries.name: Song of Glorious Invocation
entries.effect:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

You weave the true names of several runes you've drawn into a beautiful song, invoking them all simultaneously. Choose up to three rune-bearers within 30 feet and Invoke one Rune on each of them. The song also inspires the rune-bearers, granting them a +1 status bonus to skill checks and saves against fear effects for 1 minute.

Effect: Song Of Glorious Invocation

entries.name: Terrifying Invocation
entries.effect: You spit and roar as you pronounce your rune's terrible name. You attempt to [[/act demoralize]] a single target within 30 feet and then Invoke one Rune upon that target. You don't take a penalty to your check if the creature doesn't understand your language.

entries.name: Transpose Etching
entries.effect: With a pinching gesture, you pick up a word and move it elsewhere. You move any one of your runes within 30 feet to a different eligible target within 30 feet.

entries.name: Writing On the Wall
entries.effect:
You place hidden messages written in a runic cipher of your devising. You can cast Embed Message once per day as an innate spell. The rank of this spell is equal to half your level, rounded up, and the tradition can be any tradition for which you are at least expert in the related skill (Arcana for arcane, Nature for primal, Occultism for occult, and Religion for divine). When you cast embed message, instead of choosing a language you know for the message's text and speech, you can choose to have the message be text only, written in a runic code that only you know. You can impart the knowledge of this code to up to 5 creatures over the course of 10 minutes; they retain this knowledge indefinitely, but you can devise a new runic code for subsequent messages you wish to be encoded.

A creature can Decipher the Writing of your runic code using the same skill associated with the chosen tradition against your class DC.

entries.name: Diacritic Fluency
entries.effect:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

When you intensify your attention, you can modify a rune with great speed. The next time you Trace a Rune this turn, you can also Trace a diacritic Rune on that rune.

entries.name: Engraving Maneuver
entries.effect:
Requirements You are wielding a melee weapon with the disarm, shove, or trip trait.

After quickly drawing a rune on your weapon, you can transfer the rune to a foe as you knock them down, push them away, or disarm their weapon. Attempt to [[/act disarm]], [[/act shove]], or [[/act trip]] a target; your weapon must have the corresponding trait. If your skill check is successful, you Trace a Rune onto the target of the Strike even if the target is pushed out of range.

entries.name: Runic Reprisal
entries.effect: When you Raise your Shield, you can bury a runic trap into it, which is set off by the clash of an enemy weapon. When you use Fortifying Knock, you can Trace a Rune with a damaging invocation on your shield, even if it normally couldn't be applied to a shield. The traced rune doesn't have its normal effect, instead fading into your shield. If you Shield Block with the shield against a melee Strike, you can Invoke the Rune as part of the reaction, causing the rune to detonate outward and apply its invocation effect to the attacking creature.

entries.name: Tracing Trance
entries.effect:
Trigger Your turn begins.

Your hands flow unbidden, tracing runes as if by purest instinct. You become Quickened until the end of your turn and can use the extra action only to Trace a Rune (including to supply 1 action if using the 2-action version of Trace Rune). Focused on the act of creation, you can't use invocation actions this turn.

entries.name: Vital Compound Invocation
entries.effect: You can invoke runes from traditions that manipulate vital energy to restore flesh. You Invoke two Runes—one must be a divine rune, and one must be a primal rune. In addition to the runes' normal effects, one creature that's within 30 feet of both invoked runes regains Hit Points equal to 5 + double your level (Level*2)+5)[Healing]).

entries.name: Words, Fly Free
entries.effect:
Requirements Your Runic Tattoo is not faded.

Just because your runes are tattooed on your very body doesn't mean they need to remain there. You fling your hand out, the rune from your Runic Tattoo flowing down it and flying through the air in a crescent. You Trace the Rune onto all targets within a Type:Cone|Distance:15 that match the rune's usage requirement. The rune then returns to you, faded.

entries.name: Drawn In Vital Ink
entries.effect:
Requirements During your last action, you succeeded at a melee Strike that dealt physical damage to a creature that can bleed.

After striking the target, you run a brush or finger along your weapon to collect a bit of its blood. For the next minute, you can Trace a Rune targeting the creature you drew blood from at a range of 60 feet (even if you're Tracing a Rune as a single action). Using Drawn in Vital Ink against a different creature requires you to wipe off the blood already on your weapon, ending the effect for the previous creature.

entries.name: Edifying Trace
entries.effect:
When you apply a rune to a foe, it reveals something about them to you. Trace a Rune onto an adjacent enemy and then attempt a skill check to Recall Knowledge about that target. If you succeed, you leverage this knowledge when you invoke any of your runes on that target; that target takes a –1 status penalty to saving throws against your invocations for 1 minute.

If you use Edifying Trace on another enemy, the effect ends for the previous enemy.

entries.name: Elemental Revision
entries.effect: You can scratch out and rewrite part of an elemental rune to temporarily change the type of power it channels. You touch an adjacent Corrosive, Flaming, Frost, Shock, or Thundering rune on an unattended item or one held or worn by a willing creature, and you change it to any other rune from that list. You can also revise the greater version of any of the above runes into the greater version of any other rune on the list (for instance, Greater Corrosive into Greater Frost). The revision lasts for 1 minute before the rune's original magic reasserts itself.

entries.name: Swiping Trace
entries.effect:
You prepare a rune on the end of your weapon so that it transfers to your enemies. Make a melee Strike and compare the attack roll to the AC of up to two enemies within your melee reach. Roll damage only once and apply it to each creature you hit. You can Trace a Rune on each creature you hit and deal damage to, but they must be the same rune. A Swiping Trace counts as two attacks for your multiple attack penalty.

If you're using a weapon with the sweep trait, its bonus applies to your Swiping Trace attack.

entries.name: Nimble Dodge
entries.effect:
Trigger A creature targets you with an attack and you can see the attacker.

Requirements You are not encumbered.

You deftly dodge out of the way, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

entries.name: Overextending Feint
entries.effect:
You goad a foe into overextending. On a successful Feint, you can use the following success and critical success effects instead of any other effects that would occur when you Feint.

Critical Success The target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to all attack rolls against you before the end of its next turn.

Success The target takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its next attack roll against you before the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Plant Evidence
entries.effect: You can put a single item you're holding of light or negligible Bulk onto a person without them noticing by succeeding at a Thievery|Defense:Perception check against their Perception DC. If you have the ruffian racket, you can do this as a free action when you successfully Shove a target.

entries.name: Tumble Behind (Rogue)
entries.effect: You tumble under and behind your foe, your rapid movement letting you catch them off guard. When you successfully [[/act tumble-through]], the foe whose space you passed through is Off Guard against the next attack you make before the end of your turn.

entries.name: Twin Feint
entries.effect:
Requirements You are wielding two melee weapons, each in a different hand.

You use an attack with one weapon to distract your foe from a second attack coming at a different angle. Make one Strike with each of your two melee weapons, both against the same target. The target is automatically Off Guard against the second attack. Apply your multiple attack penalty to the Strikes normally.

entries.name: Deny Support
entries.effect:
Access Help either the Washboard Dogs or the Diobel Sweepers destroy their rival.

When you succeed or critically succeed at a Deception check to Feint an opponent, that target can't flank with their allies until the beginning of your next turn.

entries.name: Eldritch Debilitations
entries.effect:
You know how to apply debilitations that are particularly troublesome for spellcasters. Add the following debilitations to the list you can choose from when you use Debilitating Strike.

  • Debilitation The target is Stupefied 1.
  • Debilitation The target can't Step.

entries.name: Heartless Debilitations
entries.effect:
You debilitate your enemies with ruthless and terrifying efficiency. Add the following debilitations to the list you can choose from when you use Debilitating Strike.

  • Debilitation The target gains weakness 5 to bleed and poison damage.

  • Debilitation The target becomes Frightened 1.

entries.name: Methodical Debilitations
entries.effect:
You strategically craft your debilitations to lessen or negate an enemy's tactical advantages. Add the following debilitations to the list you can choose from when you use Debilitating Strike.

  • Debilitation The target can't flank or contribute to allies' flanking. Effect: Methodical Debilitations (Flanking)
  • Debilitation The target doesn't gain a circumstance bonus to AC from Raising a Shield, lesser cover, or standard cover; it gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC only from greater cover or Taking Cover. Effect: Methodical Debilitations (Cover)

entries.name: Nimble Strike
entries.effect: You're cunning enough to find an opening in an opponent's attack. When you use your Nimble Dodge reaction, you can make a melee Strike against the triggering creature. This Strike doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike. If you use the Nimble Roll feat, you can make this Strike at any point during your roll.

entries.name: Precise Debilitations
entries.effect:
You attack with great precision. Add the following debilitations to the list you can choose from when you use Debilitating Strike.

  • Debilitation The target takes an additional 2d6 precision damage from your attacks. Effect: Precise Debilitations
  • Debilitation The target becomes Off Guard.

entries.name: Sneak Adept
entries.effect: It's almost impossible to spot you. When you roll a failure on a Sneak action, you get a success instead. You can still critically fail.

entries.name: Tactical Debilitations
entries.effect:
You learn new debilitations that grant you tactical advantages against your foes. Add the following debilitations to the list you can choose from when you use Debilitating Strike.

  • Debilitation The target can't use reactions.
  • Debilitation The target can't flank or contribute to allies' flanking. Effect: Tactical Debilitations (No Flanking)

entries.name: Vicious Debilitations
entries.effect:
The debilitations you dish out seriously impair your foes. Add the following debilitations to the list you can choose from when you use Debilitating Strike.

  • Debilitation The target gains weakness 5 to your choice of bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. Effect: Vicious Debilitations
  • Debilitation The target becomes Clumsy 1.

entries.name: Bloody Debilitation
entries.effect:
Your attacks slice arteries and veins. Add the following debilitation to the list you can choose from when you use Debilitating Strike.

  • Debilitation The target takes 3D6[Bleed] damage.

entries.name: Coordinated Distraction
entries.effect:
Access Help either the Washboard Dogs or the Diobel Sweepers destroy their rival.

With a sharp whistle or wave of your hands, you distract an opponent from the fact that one of your allies is about to attack them. Choose a target and an ally, both of whom must be within 30 feet. The target is Off Guard against the first Strike the ally makes on their next turn; if your ally doesn't Strike that target, the effect is lost. Depending on how you describe your distraction, this action gains either the auditory or visual trait.

entries.name: Critical Debilitation
entries.effect:
Your debilitations are especially effective on your most powerful attacks. Whenever you critically succeed at an attack roll against an enemy and use Debilitating Strike, add the following debilitation to the list you can choose from.

  • Debilitation The target attempts a Fortitude|Against:Rogue save against your class DC with the following effects.

    Critical Success The target is unaffected.

    Success The target is Slowed 1 until the end of your next turn.

    Failure The target is Slowed 2 until the end of your next turn.

    Critical Failure The target is Paralyzed until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Deadly Poison Weapon
entries.effect:
Your poisons are devastatingly potent. When you apply a simple poison with Poison Weapon, the poison deals 4D4[Poison] damage instead of 1d4 poison damage.

When you apply an injury poison to your weapon, the DC to resist that poison increases by 2, to a maximum of your class DC.

entries.name: Fantastic Leap
entries.effect:
You launch yourself through the air at a foe. Attempt a High Jump or Long Jump. If you attempt a High Jump, determine the height of your jump as though determining the length of a Long Jump. At the end of your jump, you can make a melee Strike.

After your Strike, you fall to the ground if you're in the air. If the distance of your fall is no more than the height of your jump, you take no damage and land upright.

entries.name: Felling Shot
entries.effect:
Your ranged attacks can shoot an unprepared foe right out of the air. Make a ranged Strike against an Off Guard creature. If the Strike is a success and deals damage, the target must attempt a Reflex|Against:Rogue save against your class DC.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The target falls up to 120 feet. If it hits the ground, it takes no damage from the fall.

Critical Failure As failure, and the target can't fly, jump, levitate, or otherwise leave the ground until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Preparation
entries.effect: You survey the battlefield, calculating the possibilities. You gain one additional reaction, which you can use before the beginning of your next turn for any rogue reaction.

entries.name: Ricochet Feint
entries.effect: While in Ricochet Stance, you can bounce a thrown weapon off a foe to distract them. You can attempt a Feint against a creature within the first range increment of a thrown weapon you are wielding, rather than only creatures within your melee reach.

entries.name: Spring from the Shadows
entries.effect: You leap from hiding and assail your target. You Stride up to your Speed, but you must end your movement next to an enemy you're Hidden from or Undetected by. You then Strike that enemy; you remain hidden from or undetected by that creature until after you Strike. You can use Spring from the Shadows while Burrowing, Climbing, Flying, or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

entries.name: Defensive Roll
entries.effect:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

Trigger A physical attack would reduce you to 0 Hit Points.

Dropping into a roll to disperse the force of the blow, you can partially evade a lethal attack and stay conscious. You take half damage from the triggering attack

entries.name: Instant Opening
entries.effect: You distract your opponent with a few choice words or a rude gesture. Choose a target within 30 feet. It's Off Guard against your attacks until the end of your next turn. Depending on the way you describe your distraction, this action gains either the auditory or visual trait.

entries.name: Leave an Opening
entries.effect: When you hit hard enough, you leave an opening so your ally can jump in on the action. Whenever you critically hit an Off Guard opponent with a melee attack and deal damage, the target triggers a Reactive Strike reaction from one ally of your choice who has that reaction, as if the enemy had used a manipulate action.

entries.name: Stay Down!
entries.effect:
Trigger A Prone foe within your reach Stands.

You have ways of keeping your foes down. Attempt an Athletics|Defense:Fortitude check against the triggering foe's Fortitude DC. On a success, the action is disrupted, causing the creature to remain prone. On a critical success, the creature also can't Stand until its next turn.

entries.name: Blank Slate
entries.effect: Your deceptions confound even the most powerful magic that could spy on you. Detection, revelation, and scrying effects pass right over you, your possessions, and your auras, detecting nothing unless the detecting effect has a counteract rank of 10 or higher. For example, Detect Magic would still detect other magic in the area but not any magic on you, Truesight wouldn't reveal you, Locate or Scrying wouldn't find you, and so on.

entries.name: Cloud Step
entries.effect: Using fantastic acrobatic skill, you can walk for brief stretches across insubstantial surfaces. When you Stride, you can move across water, air, and solid surfaces that can hold only limited weight as if they were normal ground. If you Stride over a trap with a weight-sensitive pressure plate, you don't trigger it. At the end of your turn, you sink, fall, break fragile surfaces, or trigger traps as normal for your current location.

entries.name: Cognitive Loophole
entries.effect:
Trigger Your turn ends.

Requirements You are currently affected by a mental effect.

You can find a loophole in a mental effect to temporarily overcome it. Until the end of your next turn, you ignore a single mental effect. You can suppress a particular effect using Cognitive Loophole only once. You can't use Cognitive Loophole to suppress an effect you chose to have affect you.

Special You can use this reaction even if the mental effect is preventing you from using reactions.

entries.name: Cutthroat Grapple
entries.effect:
Trigger A creature attempts to Escape from your Sawtooth Grapple.

You can punish a creature that tries to escape your blades. Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature. On a hit, the creature takes a –4 circumstance penalty to its Escape attempt and 1d6 bleed damage.

Effect: Cutthroat Grapple

entries.name: Dispelling Slice
entries.effect: Your sneak attack slices through the threads binding magic to a target. Make a Strike against an Off Guard creature. If your Strike deals sneak attack damage, you attempt to counteract a single spell of your choice active on the target. Your counteract rank is equal to half your level (rounded up), and your counteract check modifier is equal to your class DC – 10.

entries.name: Perfect Distraction
entries.effect: You use clever tactics to mislead your foes as you sneak away. You Sneak while leaving a decoy behind. The decoy acts as the spell Mislead, though you aren't Invisible, just Undetected. You can continue to concentrate to move your decoy, as with the spell, whether or not you remain Hidden throughout the duration. Once you use Perfect Distraction, you need to spend 10 minutes to set up another decoy before you can use it again.

entries.name: Steal Spell
entries.effect:
When you use Legendary Thief to steal the impossible, you can steal a prepared spell or spontaneous spell from a foe. The spell is randomly selected from the highest-rank spells the foe knows that have a target or area, to a maximum of 8th-rank spells; the target loses the appropriate spell slot as if they had cast it themself.

You can Cast the Spell once within the next [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}, after which the fleeting magic fades; this otherwise works the same as casting a Loaner Spell.

entries.name: Swift Elusion
entries.effect:
Trigger A foe ends its movement adjacent to you.

Attempt an Acrobatics|Defense:Reflex check against the foe's Reflex DC. If you succeed, either Stride to a different space adjacent to the foe or move the foe to a different space adjacent to you.

entries.name: Implausible Infiltration
entries.effect:
Requirements You are adjacent to a floor or vertical wall.

You find tiny imperfections and somehow fit yourself through them, possibly moving directly through the wall or floor. Your movement attempt fails if the wall or floor is made of something other than wood, plaster, or stone; is thicker than 10 feet; or contains even a thin layer of metal. If you have a climb Speed, you can use this ability to attempt to move through a ceiling.

entries.name: Implausible Purchase (Rogue)
entries.effect: You can use Prescient Planner even if you have already used it after purchasing goods, and you can Interact to draw the item as a single action instead of a 2-action activity. In addition, five times per day, you can use Prescient Planner to pull out a common consumable item up to 6 levels lower than your level.

entries.name: Powerful Sneak
entries.effect: You've learned to exploit your enemies' openings. Your sneak attack damage ignores any immunity or resistance the target has to precision damage. In addition, when you Sneak, you can designate one creature you're undetected by at the end of that action. On the next attack you make against that creature before the end of your next turn, any sneak attack die you roll that's less than 3 is a 3 instead.
